planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Gold Tide requires full sun for maximum flower production and stays much lower and wider than standard forsythia.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Gold Tide is a true dwarf, low-mounding, spreading forsythia, staying under three feet tall while spreading considerably wider, unlike the tall, upright, arching habit of classic forsythia cultivars like Lynwood Gold. It produces the same brilliant, abundant, bright yellow flowers smothering bare branches in earliest spring before the leaves emerge, giving a groundcover-scale burst of early color for a bank, border edge, or foundation planting where a full-sized forsythia would be too large. Prune immediately after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds form on the previous year's wood and later pruning removes next spring's bloom.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; its low, spreading habit suits it to mass planting, a border edge, or a large container.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Yuki Snowflake is the white-flowered sibling of Yuki Cherry Blossom, bred from the same true-dwarf, groundcover-habit line of slender deutzia, covering itself in a dense flush of small, star-shaped, pure white flowers in late spring above compact, fine-textured foliage. Its low, spreading habit fills in quickly for mass plantings, border edges, and slopes, and it holds a tidy mounded shape without pruning. Like other deutzia it blooms on the previous year's wood, so any shaping should be done right after flowering to avoid removing next season's buds. It tolerates a range of soils once established and requires little maintenance beyond an occasional light shaping.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; good drainage helps prevent the root problems weigela can develop in heavy, waterlogged soil.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade. Ghost produces pale, almost luminous cream-white funnel-shaped flowers over pale green to chartreuse foliage in a heavy late-spring flush, a softer, quieter color combination than the vivid pinks and reds of most weigela cultivars, making it a useful pastel accent among bolder-colored companions. Like other weigela it flowers on the previous year's wood, so prune immediately after bloom if shaping is needed, and avoid heavy pruning later in the season, which removes next year's flower buds. It tolerates heat and average garden soil well once established and needs little care beyond occasional shaping.
